verdict.rationale: Aider's scripting docs describe a headless mode: `--message` executes one natural-language instruction, applies the edits, and exits (e.g. `aider --message "..." hello.js`). They also document a Python `Coder.create(...).run(...)` API for programmatic use. Options can be set via `.aider.conf.yml` or `AIDER_xxx` environment variables, and `--test-cmd`/`--auto-test` can run tests after each edit, both of which suit CI pipelines. Missing for 10: explicit CI/pipeline integration docs or examples (e.g. auto-confirm flags, exit-code semantics for automated runs), and independent hands-on reports of CI usage; the community only mentions intending to use the scriptable mode.
